verifiedRuntimeProbe.stdoutHead:
Usage: resume-matcher <tool> [arguments]
       resume-matcher <tool> --help     the tool's description and argument schema

Arguments are one JSON object:
  '{"resume_id": "abc"}'   inline
  @args.json               read from a file
  -                        read from stdin

or any number of fields:
  key=value                a string
  key=@job.md              a string read from a file
  key:=json                any JSON value (number, true, list, object)
  key:=@data.json          any JSON value read from a file

The result is printed as JSON. Exit code 1 means the tool failed (the reason is
on stderr), 2 means the command line was wrong.

Tools:
  add_job                   Store a job description. Pass the keywords you extracted to enable scoring.
  create_application        Add a tracker card for an existing job_id or a pasted job_description.
  create_master_resume      Create a master resume from structured data you built (e.g. from extract_document_text).
  export_resume_pdf         Render a saved resume to PDF and report its page count. Needs the web frontend running. Overwrites an existing file at output_path.
  extract_document_text     Extract markdown from a local PDF/DOCX/DOC/MD/TXT file (absolute path).
  get_job                   Get a stored job description and its cached keywords.
  get_resume                Get a resume's structured data, cover letter and outreach message.
  get_resume_job            Get the job a tailored resume was tailored for.
  get_resume_schema         JSON schema for resume_data plus authoring guidance. The rules are guidance; save tools enforce only the preservation checks.
  get_status                Data location, record counts, templates and limits. Call this first.
  list_applications         List tracker cards, optionally for one status column.
  list_resumes              List resumes, newest first. Masters are the source of truth for tailoring.
  parse_check_file          ATS parse-check a local PDF or DOCX (absolute path): extractability, layout and content checks.
  parse_check_resume        ATS parse-check a saved resume as rendered with these settings, plus a round trip against its data. Writes nothing.
  recalculate_ats_score     Recompute and store a tailored resume's ATS score from its saved data and job keywords.
  save_tailored_resume      Save a tailored resume you wrote. Rejected if it breaks preservation rules.
  score_resume              Keyword match and ATS score for a saved resume or draft against job keywords.
  set_cover_letter          Store a cover letter you wrote for a resume.
  set_default_master        Make a master resume the default tailoring source.
  set_job_keywords          Attach the keywords you extracted to an existing job.
  set_outreach_message      Store an outreach message you wrote for a resume.
  set_resume_title          Rename a resume (max 80 characters).
  tailor_and_verify         Validate, save and verify a tailored resume you wrote, in one call.
  update_application        Move or edit a tracker card. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Pass null for notes, company or role to clear it, or for position to move the card to the end of its column.
  update_resume             Replace a resume's structured data. Tailored resumes get grounding warnings.
  validate_tailored_resume  Dry-run the preservation checks save_tailored_resume enforces. Writes nothing.
  verify_resume             Render a saved resume once and report page count, ATS parse-check, keyword score and issues. Writes nothing.

adoptionBoundary.reason: Use Resume-Matcher as a narrow artifact compiler/verifier. Do not create a second application-state authority; tools requiring its frontend/database become conditional consumers, not Career core.

truthBoundary: This proves the pinned stable backend CLI can be resolved and executed under the tested Python 3.13 runtime, and records a negative default-host-runtime probe. It does not prove AI-provider configuration, frontend-dependent rendering, employer truth, application state, or hiring outcomes.
